source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 15. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

learn.en: Ibrahim's people worshipped idols — statues they made with their own hands. Ibrahim saw that statues cannot hear, speak, help or harm.
learn.title: Statues can't help

learn.en: He asked them: “What are these statues you worship?” They said: “We found our fathers worshipping them.” (Qur'an 21:52–53)
learn.title: A clever question

learn.en: While they were away, he broke the idols — all except the biggest. They asked: “Who did this?” He said: “Ask the biggest one, if they can speak!” (Qur'an 21:63)
learn.title: The biggest idol

learn.en: They knew statues can't speak, but they were too proud. They threw Ibrahim into a huge fire. Allah said: “O fire, be cool and safe for Ibrahim.” (Qur'an 21:69) And he came out unharmed!
learn.title: Cool and safe

learn.en: Tawḥīd means worshipping Allah alone — the message of every prophet. Ibrahim made people think, and spoke to his father with respect.
learn.title: Tawḥīd

quiz.en: Why did Ibrahim leave the biggest idol?
What did Allah tell the fire?
opts: Be cool and safe for Ibrahim

quiz.en: True or false? Tawḥīd means worshipping Allah alone.
True or false? Ibrahim was rude to his father.

think.q: How did Ibrahim show courage AND good manners?
think.a: He stood for the truth alone, but he still spoke kindly and respectfully to his father.

parents.summary: Ibrahim stood alone for tawḥīd. He broke the idols to make people think, and Allah made the fire cool and safe for him.
parents.tip: Ask your child: “Can a toy hear you?” — then talk about why only Allah hears and helps.
